answer.reason: The after source supports preserving CHARBOUND markers for graphemes retained by STRIPCC. Mapping is a primary target operation, but the fixed harness has no map call combining those options. The same preservation behavior was unavailable before the change, so this coverage gap is introduced. Evidence: u-c2ddb5ea0940cb0a5374:641-650, u-82fb367dcb7283a12bb8:641-646, u-1f26bb9c4ca01b89207f:78-97.

With the supported setup CHARBOUND|STRIPCC, mapping strips U+0001 and preserves a boundary marker before each retained letter, yielding {0xff, 0x61, 0xff, 0x62, 0x00}. The fixed harness supplies that input to map calls, but none uses both options.

scope_contract.reason: The entry primarily maps text, including CHARBOUND mappings. The source defines CHARBOUND markers and STRIPCC control stripping as options on that mapping surface.

evidence.quote:
/** Strips and/or convers control characters.
   *
   * NLF-sequences are transformed into space, except if one of the
   * NLF2LS/PS/LF options is given. HorizontalTab (HT) and FormFeed (FF)
   * are treated as a NLF-sequence in this case.  All other control
   * characters are simply removed.
   */
  UTF8PROC_STRIPCC   = (1<<9),
  /**
   * Performs unicode case folding, to be able to do a case-insensitive
   * string comparison.
   */
  UTF8PROC_CASEFOLD  = (1<<10),
  /**
   * Inserts 0xFF bytes at the beginning of each sequence which is
   * representing a single grapheme cluster (see UAX#29).
   */
  UTF8PROC_CHARBOUND = (1<<11),
